rymattylanreitti.timetableEvidence: The timetable starts and ends journeys at Haapala, repeats Ruotsalainen on longer journeys, and lists other demand stops between the two Ruotsalainen calls.
rymattylanreitti.interpretation: Ruotsalainen is often a repeated trunk call. Other piers can be turnarounds or single calls on a branch loop; a single call alone is not proof of a ring route.

velkuanreitti.timetableEvidence: The timetable contains both Teersalo return journeys and journeys between Teersalo and Hakkenpää, with demand stops in varying order.
velkuanreitti.interpretation: Closed Teersalo journeys and terminal-to-terminal journeys must be separated. Rauhala is frequently repeated, while most other piers are called once or used as a turnaround.

nagunorra.timetableEvidence: The timetable contains journeys between Nagu and Lavarn in both directions and separate local return journeys such as Nagu-Seili-Nagu.
nagunorra.interpretation: Calls on Nagu-Lavarn journeys are terminal-to-terminal calls. Closed journeys are classified separately, including exact turnaround patterns.

nagusodra.timetableEvidence: The timetable starts and ends journeys at Kirjais and lists several groups of on-demand piers; AIS sequences contain both immediate turnarounds and longer closed journeys.
nagusodra.interpretation: Most observed piers are called once on a closed journey, but this is recorded as an observation rather than treated as proof that every service is a ring route.

hitisrutt.timetableEvidence: The service contains journeys between Kasnäs and Dalsbruk as well as separate return journeys from Kasnäs to island branches.
hitisrutt.interpretation: Terminal-to-terminal calls and closed island journeys are separated. Exact A-B-A calls are treated as turnarounds.

houtskarrutt.timetableEvidence: The route area contains several published endpoint pairs and short return branches from Kannvik.
houtskarrutt.interpretation: Each observed terminal pair is retained. Closed journeys and exact turnaround calls are modeled separately from terminal-to-terminal traffic.

korporutt.timetableEvidence: Published services connect Verkan, Havträsk and Kittuis and also include return branches from a terminal.
korporutt.interpretation: Terminal-pair direction is the primary structural key. A closed journey can contain a turnaround or a longer branch loop.

norralinjen.timetableEvidence: Ålandstrafiken publishes stop times in both directions on Hummelvik-Enklinge-Kumlinge-Lappo-Torsholma, including partial journeys starting or ending at Kumlinge.
norralinjen.interpretation: The published timetable determines the service order. AIS is used to validate driving times and realized optional calls, not to infer an alternative schedule.

sodralinjen.timetableEvidence: Ålandstrafiken publishes stop times in both directions on Galtby-Kökar-Kyrkogårdsö-Husö-Sottunga-Överö-Långnäs. Husö and Kyrkogårdsö are optional booked calls.
sodralinjen.interpretation: The published timetable determines the base journey. AIS validates realized travel and detour effects.

scheduleRules.basis: published individual delays plus confirmed route geometry

utorutt.timetableEvidence: The published timetable gives separate trips in both directions on Pärnäs-Nötö-Aspö-Jurmo-Utö.
utorutt.interpretation: The timetable determines direction and stop order. The last-year complete AIS sample is too small to infer topology independently.
